papers.title: A Riemann-Hilbert approach to the two-component modified Camassa-Holm system with step-like boundary conditions
papers.abstract: We develop a Riemann--Hilbert formalism for the Cauchy problem for the two-component modified Camassa--Holm (2-mCH) system on the real line under non-zero step-like boundary conditions. Starting from the corresponding Lax pair, we carry out the direct spectral analysis and establish the analytic, symmetry, and asymptotic properties of the eigenfunctions and spectral data determined by the initial conditions. These results are then used to formulate right and left matrix Riemann--Hilbert problems and derive parametric formulas for reconstructing both components. These formulas also use a transported profile determined by the initial ratio of the two momenta. Under suitable regularity and positivity assumptions, we show that a solution of the right Riemann--Hilbert problem, together with this profile, yields a local solution of the 2-mCH system. For a common constant background, we construct a family of smooth reflectionless solutions associated with a single pair of discrete eigenvalues. The scalar soliton, obtained when the profile vanishes, is the only travelling wave in this family.

papers.title: Liouvillian integrability of vector fields in higher dimensions
papers.abstract: We consider complex rational vector fields in dimension $n>2$ (equivalently, differential forms of degree $n-1$ in $n$ variables) which admit a Liouvillian first integral. Extending a classical result by Singer for $n=2$, our main result states that there exists a first integral which is obtained by two successive integrations from one-forms with coefficients in a finite algebraic extension of the rational function field. The proof uses Puiseux series in a novel way to simplify computations. We also apply this method to give elementary proofs of Singer's theorem for rational one-forms, and of the Prelle-Singer theorem on elementary integrability of rational vector fields.

papers.title: A Novel Algebraic Approach to Medium-Range Solvable Models
papers.abstract: We extend Jones' Baxterisation, which produces solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation directly from the generators of an algebra, to quantum spin chains with medium-range interactions. The key ingredient is an extended Yang-Baxter equation for R matrices that are built from the generators attached to two neighbouring sites. Together with the accompanying Lax operator, it gives rise to transfer matrices that are in involution up to boundary terms, exactly as in Jones' construction. We find a solution to the extended Yang-Baxter equation, of non-difference form, in terms of the generators of the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring, and obtain from it two families of medium-range lattice Hamiltonians. Thus, each representation of the algebra provides a medium-range solvable model. Using the relation between the chromatic algebra of 3-colouring and the fusion category $\mathrm{Rep}(S_3)$, we construct four such representations. They reproduce the folded XXZ model and the hard-rod deformed XXZ model, and give new medium-range models of a three-state antiferromagnet and of a Rydberg-blockade ladder. Two of the four models possess non-invertible symmetries.

papers.title: Modulation equations and coherence dynamics in a qubit chain coupled to a circulating fluxon
papers.abstract: We derive modulation equations for the joint quantum amplitudes of a circulating fluxon and an exchange-coupled qubit chain whose endpoint interacts with the field. A unitary passage operator combines the translational packet, vacuum dressing, and discrete oscillatory modes. A resonant normal form separates the slow amplitude evolution from nonresonant corrections. Ordered emission and return amplitudes generate a second-order correction that changes the population and coherence of an internal qubit. The next ground-band coefficient gives compensating diagonal and near-resonant off-diagonal contributions to the accumulated error. We bound the state error a posteriori. At a velocity-selected resonance, direct propagation over 81 passages gives a mode contribution of order $6\times10^{-8}$; the cubic ground-band approximation agrees with an expanded full calculation to $1.5\times10^{-9}$ in the tested observables. The equations describe how the source profile and field memory affect coherence inside the chain.

papers.title: Reproducing kernel and matrix representation of the deformed quantum optical density operator of $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states on $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ fermionic quantum algebra
papers.abstract: We study the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$super-coherent states with two Grassmann variables $(\zeta_1,\zeta_2)$ built on the superalgebra $\mathcal{B}_0\oplus\mathcal{B}_1$ associated with the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$deformed quantum algebras of Hounkonnou and Bukweli-Kyemba, the two dilation parameters $\phi_1(p,q)$ and $\phi_2(p,q)$ being meromorphic functions of two variables evaluated at $(p,q)$. The graded super-Fock space splits into four sectors: bosonic, $\phi_1-$fermionic, $\phi_2-$fermionic and bi-fermionic. In each of them we establish the diagonal representation of the density operator by means of the $\mathcal{R}(p,q)-$derivative, angular integration and Berezin integration, and we give a unified compact form in terms of sectorial parametric functions. The total density operator is obtained in explicit form as the sum of the four sectorial contributions, and can be read as a mixture of the four sectors. We define the sectorial reproducing kernels, obtained from the resolution of the identity, we compute the matrix elements of the density operator in the super-coherent state basis, and we prove the hermiticity, positivity and matrix multiplication properties of the kernels, together with the series expansion of their diagonal values. An integral formulation relates the density operator, its density function and the reproducing kernel, the latter being the function associated with the identity operator. Berezin quantization in the bosonic sector yields the quantized operators associated with $z$, $\bar z$, $|z|^2$, $z^2$ and $\bar z^2$ and their mean values; the dispersions of the super-position and super-momentum operators show that the super-coherent states are intelligent states.

papers.title: Darboux transformation for the ASDYM equations: Solitons and instantons
papers.abstract: Using a one-fold Darboux transformation for the anti-self-dual Yang--Mills equations, we express the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density in terms of $\tau$-functions. For solitons constructed from exponential functions, we show that the associated $\tau$-functions admit a parametrization by arbitrary points in the Grassmannian Gr(N,M;$\mathbb{C}$), and construct the corresponding Yang--Mills fields. For instantons arising from the Atiyah--Drinfeld--Hitchin--Manin (ADHM) construction, we reinterpret the ADHM construction in terms of a one-fold Darboux transformation, recover Osborn's formula for the Yang--Mills Lagrangian density, and obtain the corresponding gauge connection.

papers.title: Pfaffian solutions to the Ernst equation
papers.abstract: We obtain a Pfaffian representation of the Yamazaki-Hori solutions to the Ernst equation. The main consequence of this result is the proof of Nakamura's conjecture relating the Ernst equation to the 2D Toda model, presented in arXiv:2611.19558.

papers.title: Baker-Akhiezer realization and reconstruction for three-wave interactions in canonical multiwave Hamiltonian
papers.abstract: We revisit the canonical multiwave Hamiltonians with three-wave interactions studied by Menyuk, Chen and Lee, and by Jiang, Rauch-Wojciechowski and Bullough. With compatible linear phase terms, we construct their general solution on the generic spectral locus from multipoint Baker-Akhiezer functions. Conversely, we give a finite interpolation criterion and completion procedure that realize prescribed Baker-Akhiezer evaluations on arbitrary smooth algebraic curves in the same Hamiltonian system. We identify the prescribed curve with the normalized spectral curve and show that commuting polynomial Hamiltonians span every Abel direction on each birational spectral level, including the accompanying mode phases. Together, these results establish a correspondence between Baker-Akhiezer data and canonical multiwave dynamics, supporting our view of this system as a fundamental canonical Hamiltonian setting for Baker-Akhiezer functions. We make explicit its connections with other established integrable systems and validate hyperelliptic, trigonal and multipuncture examples numerically.

papers.title: Integrable discretization of the Maxwell-Bloch equations
papers.abstract: Numerical schemes for the Maxwell-Bloch equations keep the length of the Bloch vector but not the integrable structure, so that solitons are only approximate solutions. We write an integrable discretization, in both time and space, of these equations for a complex field in a resonant two-level medium in the physical variables and use it as a numerical scheme. The lattice follows from a discrete Lax pair with the analytic structure of the continuous one; an auxiliary field variable is fixed by an isospectral normalization, and the resulting scheme is explicit, a $2\times2$ similarity transformation of the density matrix per grid node. It conserves the length of every Bloch vector and satisfies an exact energy balance between field and medium. The lattice coincides with a known fully discrete integrable system, which we use to obtain closed-form solitons and breathers; they are reflectionless potentials with energy $16\sum_j\mathrm{Im}\,\lambda_j$ and converge to the McCall-Hahn soliton and Lamb's breather. Inhomogeneous broadening is included through ordered sublayers that keep integrability. On a finite time window the scattering data evolve by a closed map, with the final state of the medium given by the data at one point of the spectral plane. On the infinite line, if the medium returns to its ground state behind the pulse (which we show on the first row and observe numerically on later rows), the transmission coefficient is conserved and the reflection coefficient evolves linearly, with the multiplier of the linearized lattice. As a numerical method the lattice is explicit and second order, with a cost per accuracy comparable to that of Cayley and exponential-midpoint schemes, and an area-preserving input map with a calibrated medium coupling makes it exact for a chosen soliton.

papers.title: Weakly Nonlinear Whitham Modulation and Dispersive Shock Waves in the Modified Gardner Equation
papers.abstract: We investigate weakly nonlinear Whitham modulation and dispersive shock waves (DSWs) in a modified Gardner equation. A three-equation modulation system is derived through a Stokes expansion and averaged conservation laws. Perturbative analysis of its characteristic structure provides explicit conditions for hyperbolicity and genuine nonlinearity, and identifies a wavenumber-dependent transition between real and complex characteristic splitting. The dispersive resolution of compressive Riemann data is examined using DSW fitting, yielding analytical predictions for the harmonic- and solitary-wave edge velocities. The solitary-wave prediction is further supported by a traveling-wave energy analysis. Numerical continuation of the modulation characteristics identifies the limitations of the weakly nonlinear approximation, while direct numerical simulations using a Fourier pseudospectral method confirm close agreement with the predicted leading-edge velocity and the leading solitary-wave amplitude for the resolved cases. These results clarify the weakly nonlinear characteristic structure and the edge dynamics of dispersive shocks for the modified Gardner equation.

papers.title: Duality of operator Frobenius algebras and solution of Eisenhart-St\"ackel problem in the non-diagonal case
papers.abstract: We study Frobenius algebras of operator fields and introduce a novel notion of duality for them. We show that, under the assumption that the operator fields forming the Frobenius algebra are mutual symmetries, the operator fields in the dual Frobenius algebra are also mutual symmetries. This result allows one to construct new infinite-dimensional integrable systems of hydrodynamic type starting from a given one. As the main application, we solve the long-standing Eisenhart--St\"ackel problem for any Segre characteristic and in arbitrary dimension: namely, we describe all nondegenerate finite-dimensional integrable systems whose integrals are quadratic in momenta such that the corresponding $(1,1)$-tensors commute as operator fields.

papers.title: The 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model
papers.abstract: We develop the 1+1D $\mathcal{N}{=}2$ Wess--Zumino model with a central extension, starting from Wigner's theorem and the supertranslation group. The unitary representations of the group leads to the SUSY algebra of the generators and an extension of the group to include a central charge $Z$. We then derive a general boson/fermion mass-degeneracy theorem and construct the covariant derivative and a candidate action realizing this algebra, first for the vacuum ($Z=0$) sector and then for $Z\neq0$, where the central extension's own coordinate $\xi$ is treated explicitly. Compactifying $\xi$ gives a Kaluza--Klein tower of massive multiplets with quantized central charge, while the kink survives intact as the tower's zero mode, saturating the general BPS bound $M\geq|Z|$ derived along the way. This is a pedagogical re-derivation, aimed at a reader's first encounter with these ideas, not a new result.

papers.title: Comment on "Space-time shifted solitons and solution interactions for a generalized nonlocal nonlinear Schr\"odinger equation"
papers.abstract: Zhou and Yu [Appl. Math. Lett. 178 (2026) 109937] studied the space-time shifted NLS equation $iq_t(x,t)=q_{xx}(x,t)-2\sigma q^2(x,t) \bar{q}(x_0-x,t_0+\lambda t),\,\, \lambda=\pm 1$. They claimed that for both choices of $\lambda$ the equation is integrable. For $\lambda=-1$, however, the equation is not compatible with the standard NLS system and hence is not an integrable reduction of that system. The Hirota expansion used in the commented article does not truncate as stated; consequently the given one-soliton solution is not a solution for $\lambda=-1$. For $\lambda=1$, consistency of the shifted reduction of NLS system requires $t_0=0$ as a mandatory condition. This condition is not reported; instead $t_0$ is incorrectly treated as an arbitrary constant in the paper. The notation used in the Hirota form is misleading, and we provide a corrected form. Additionally, the equivalence between nonlocal equations with real shifts and their unshifted counterparts under translation of independent variables is clarified.
